firstPlayer.again: Lift every finger, then touch and hold to play again.

puzzle.choosing: Click, clack… the puzzle is taking shape…

cauldron.choosing: Bubble, bubble… the potion is brewing…
cauldron.picked: The potion has chosen! {color}, you go first!

quantum.choosing: Quantum chaos… tap to collapse it!
ufo.title: The UFO Abduction
arena.title: Finger Arena
setup.startNewMessage: This replaces the saved {game} session on this device.
setup.needNames: Give every player a name first.
players.title: Players
play.resetMessage: Player names stay. All scores are cleared.
play.saveImageSaved: Score sheet saved. Check Downloads or your photo gallery.
play.saveImageFailed: Could not save the score sheet.
play.finishedMessage: This game is finished. You can still review the sheet.
play.targetReachedMessage: You can keep playing or finish the game when you are ready.
score.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 3-VP disc and job market token rows to toggle them.
score.historyEmptyMessage: Add the first round to get started.
game.gwt.name: Great Western Trail
game.gwt.description: You are ranchers driving cattle from Texas to Kansas City, then shipping them west by train. Each loop around the trail you hire cowboys, craftsmen, and engineers, put up buildings, and chase a stronger herd. When the job market fills, everyone scores the same categories as the official First Edition pad.
game.gwt2.name: Great Western Trail Second Edition
game.gwt2.description: Wrangle your herd of cows across the prairie and deliver it to Kansas City. Second Edition adds solo play, new art by Chris Quilliams, Simmental cattle, extra buildings, exchange tokens, and new station master tiles.
game.gwt2.stationMastersHelper: Score each station master in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 1 VP per worker in your worker section (including printed); 3 VP per 2 objective cards in your area (fulfilled or not); 3 VP per 2 hazards; 3 VP per green+orange outlaw pair; 3 VP per 2 certificates; 3 VP per 2 station discs; 2 VP per private building on the board.
game.gwta.name: Great Western Trail Argentina
game.gwta.description: Travel the plains of the Pampas with your cattle and deliver them to Buenos Aires. Argentina adds ships, city maps, farmer tiles, exhaustion cards, and new station master tiles.
game.gwta.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 2-VP disc and job market token rows to toggle them.
game.gwta.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 pesos becomes 1 victory point. Leftover pesos do not score.
game.gwta.shipsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on the ships. Negative VP are subtracted. The total can be negative.
game.gwta.cityMapsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on the city maps. Most quays also score VP per disc.
game.gwta.stationsHelper: Sum the VP printed next to each train station that has your disc. Extra markers on the final station score that station again.
game.gwta.farmersHelper: 2 VP for each farmer tile in front of you. Do not count farmer tiles on your player board.
game.gwta.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add VP on exhaustion cards and cattle cards. Subtract any negative VP.
game.gwta.stationMastersHelper: Score each station master in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 3 VP per 2 discs left on ships; 3 VP per 2 objective cards in your area; 4 VP per set of gaucho, carpenter, engineer, and farmer; 1 VP per cattle card of breeding value 3–5; 3 VP per 2 station discs (last station once); 3 VP per 2 workers with a strength icon; 1 VP per farmer tile in front of you (not on your board); 1 VP per 2 private buildings on the board.
game.gwtep.name: Great Western Trail El Paso
game.gwtep.description: A shorter standalone Great Western Trail. Drive your herd along the trail to El Paso, hire workers, build, and ship your cattle by train to the trading posts, then score the 7 categories of the pad.
game.gwtep.footnote: Highest total wins. 5 dollars = 1 VP. Ties: most leftover dollars.
game.gwtep.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the game end row to give its 2 VP to the player who triggered it.
game.gwtep.buildingsHelper: Sum the VP printed on the buildings you own.
game.gwtep.tradingPostsHelper: Sum the VP for each of your discs on a highlighted trading post space.
game.gwtep.workersHelper: From your draw stack, hand, discard pile and worker area, add the VP printed on your worker cards.
game.gwtep.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, discard pile and worker area, add the VP printed on your cattle cards. If your herder is on the Simmental space, add 2 VP to the total.
game.gwtep.bonusTilesHelper: Sum the VP shown on the bonus tiles you own.
game.gwtep.objectivesHelper: Check your objective tiles and total the VP of those you completed. Each item can only count towards one objective, so two objectives needing the same thing need two of it. Partial or uncompleted objectives score nothing.
game.gwtnz.name: Great Western Trail New Zealand
game.gwtnz.description: Run a sheep station on the South Island of New Zealand. Breed better sheep, raise the value of your wool, and ship it from the harbours to trading posts around the world.
game.gwtnz.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 3-VP disc and bonus tiles token rows to toggle them.
game.gwtnz.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 pounds becomes 1 victory point. Leftover pounds do not score.
game.gwtnz.tradingPostsHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on all trading post crests (local, foreign, and wool). Negative VP are subtracted. The total can be negative.
game.gwtnz.harboursHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs and storehouses on small and medium harbours of the sea routes board.
game.gwtnz.pathfinderHelper: Enter the VP unlocked by your disc on the pathfinder track (shown next to or below your disc, at the most recent unlocked VP space).
game.gwtnz.hazardsHelper: Sum the VP printed on the hazard tiles and bonus tiles in front of you. Negative VP are subtracted.
game.gwtnz.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add the VP on sheep cards and bonus cards (except bonus objective cards).
game.gwtnz.stationMastersHelper: Score each harbourmaster tile in front of you. These tasks are independent of objective cards: 1 VP per certificate (permanent or temporary); 1 VP per 2 storehouses on the sea routes board; 1 VP per objective card in your area (fulfilled or not); 1 VP per private building on the board; 1 VP per hazard tile; 1 VP per card in your deck showing a ferry (including Set 1 bonus cards); 2 VP per 5 spaces advanced on the pathfinder track; 1 VP per 2 worker tiles in your worker section (including printed ones).
game.gwtnz.playerBoardHelper: 4 VP for each worker on the 5th space of any worker row. Add 2 and/or 4 VP if you cleared the matching pair of storehouses on your player board.
gwt.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points. Tap the 3-VP disc and job market token rows to toggle them.
gwt.coinsHelper: Enter cash. Every 5 dollars becomes 1 victory point. Leftover dollars do not score.
gwt.randomizer.hint: Each private building uses side A or B. All players use the same sides.
gwt.randomizer.publicHint: Shuffle the {n} public buildings onto board spaces A–{last}. For a first game, place each tile on its matching letter.
gwt.bonusCards.hint: Draws 4 of the 10 bonus card sets. Stack them below the bonus cards tiles in set-number order: the lowest set below the steering wheel, then the barrel and the bell, and the highest below the compass.
gwt.startingResources.pathfinderNote: Then, on your first turn, move a disc from a white-cornered space on your player board onto space 0 of the pathfinder track.
gwt.workerCards.title: Worker Cards
gwt.workerCards.note: Each player places these 4 below their player board, in their worker area.
gwt.startingCards.title: Starting Cards
gwt.startingCards.exhaustionNote: Each starting deck also contains 1 Exhaustion card. Shuffle it in before you draw.
gwt.startingResources.cardsNote: Draw the cards from your own shuffled player deck.
gwt.startingResources.discardNote: Players {list}: discard down to {limit} cards at the start of your first turn.
gwt.startingResources.exchangeTokenNote: Playing with this expansion? Each player also receives 1 exchange token.
gwt.buildingsHelper: Sum the VP printed on your private building tiles on the board.
gwt.deliveriesHelper: Sum the VP unlocked by your discs on city crests. Kansas City discs are −6 each. The total can be negative.
gwt.stationsHelper: Sum the VP printed next to each train station that has your disc.
gwt.hazardsHelper: Sum the VP printed on hazard tiles in front of you.
gwt.cattleHelper: From your draw stack, hand, and discard pile, add the VP printed on cattle cards.
gwt.objectivesHint: Leftover deck cards: add or drop; unmet subtract
gwt.objectivesHelper: Objective cards still in your deck can be added to your area or removed from the game (no immediate action). Then score your area: fulfilled cards add their VP, incomplete cards subtract theirs. The total can be negative.
gwt.stationMastersHelper: Score the individual tasks on station master tiles in front of you. Those tasks are independent of objective cards.
gwt.playerBoardHelper: 4 VP for each worker on the 5th or 6th space of any worker row (max 24).
game.arnak.name: Lost Ruins of Arnak
game.arnak.description: Lead an expedition onto the uncharted island of Arnak. Equip your team, uncover artifacts and archaeological sites, overcome guardians, and piece together research that may reveal the Lost Temple. After five rounds, score the same categories as the official pad.
game.arnak.footnote: Highest total wins. If tied, the first to the Lost Temple wins. If no one reached it, highest Research wins.
arnak.padHint: Tap a cell to enter points.
arnak.researchHelper: Add the points for each research token from its row. A magnifying glass in the Lost Temple scores based on the order it arrived.
arnak.templeTilesHelper: Sum the points printed on each temple tile you collected.
arnak.idolsHelper: 3 points per idol, even if it is in a slot. Then add the points printed in any empty idol slots.
arnak.guardiansHelper: 5 points for each guardian you overcame, whether you used the boon or not.
arnak.cardsHelper: Sum the points in the lower-right corner of each item and artifact in your deck, hand, and play area.
arnak.fearHelper: Fear cards score −1 each. If you have fear tiles, they score −2 each. Enter the total as a negative number.
arnak.darkTabletsHint: Altar majorities minus the cost of used dark tablets
arnak.altars.title: Altars & Dark Tablets
arnak.altars.intro: Enter how many dark tablets each player placed on each altar (0–3). The player with the most tablets on an altar gains its points. Ties are friendly: every tied player gains them.
arnak.altars.supply: {used} of {total} dark tablets used · {emptied} supply spaces emptied · each used tablet scores {per}
arnak.altars.overSupply: That is more tablets than the supply holds ({total}). Check the counts.
arnak.altars.rulesTitle: Scoring dark tablets: the cost of ambition
arnak.altars.rule1: 1. Return unused tablets. Any dark tablets players have left at the end of the game go back to the supply. Each space holds as many tablets as there are players.
arnak.altars.rule2: 2. Score negative points. The rightmost empty space of the dark tablet supply sets how many points each used tablet costs. For example, if that space shows 3, players lose 3 points for each dark tablet they played on altars.
arnak.altars.rule3: 3. Score altars. For each altar, the player who placed the most dark tablets on it gains the points printed above it. If there is a tie, all tied players gain those points.
arnak.altars.tip: Tip: Invoking altars can cost you points, but it gives big advantages during play. To offset the losses, pay attention to who has the most tablets on each altar.
arnak.leadersHint: Playing with the Expedition Leaders? Pick a unique leader for each player.
arnak.draft.hint: Add players and pick their colors, then each player gets {n} different leaders to choose from. No leader is offered to two players.
arnak.lostTempleTitle: Who reached the Lost Temple first?
arnak.lostTempleMessage: {names} are tied. Choose who got to the Lost Temple first.
arnak.lostTempleNoneHint: Highest Research among the tied players wins. If those are tied too, they share the win.
arnak.startingDeck.title: Your Starting Deck (Base Game)
arnak.startingDeck.leadersNote: Playing with leaders from the expansions? Each leader has a different starting deck, so use the leader's setup instead.
arnak.startingDeck.body: Each player has their own deck, and all decks start the same. Your deck should have the 4 basic cards in your color, plus 2 Fear cards:
game.cobse.name: The Castles of Burgundy Special Edition
game.cobse.description: Settle estates in the Duchy of Burgundy. Across five phases you draft tiles, complete colored regions, sell goods, and climb the victory track. The Special Edition adds solo play and the expansion tiles.
cob.quickReference.hint: Tap the sheet to turn it over.
cob.quickReference.pinch: Pinch to zoom in and out.
cob.quickReference.drag: Drag on the sheet to magnify a detail.
cob.duchy.label: Duchy
cob.duchy.hint.base: Each player draws one random duchy and chooses a side. The five double-sided boards are numbered 1–10, and each board has four copies. Sides 1 and 2 are the beginner duchy.
cob.duchy.hint.firstGame: For a first game, every player takes the beginner duchy and the same number, 1 or 2. Place the starting castle on the center space numbered 6.
cob.duchy.hint.firstExpansion: Each player receives one random duchy numbered 11–18. These are four double-sided boards, with four copies of each.
cob.duchy.hint.championship: The 2013 and 2016 championship boards are the two sides of one duchy, numbered 19 and 20. The box has four copies.
cob.duchy.hint.specialEdition: The Special Edition duchy is numbered 21 and 22, with four copies. Each player chooses a side.
cob.duchy.hint.borderPosts: Each player receives one random duchy numbered 23–30. The border posts are on the player board, so this expansion can also be played with any other duchy.
cob.duchy.hint.team: Each team uses halves 31a and 32a. The other side, 31b and 32b, is the advanced team board.
cob.duchy.hint.solo: The solo game uses one duchy. Side 33 is for beginning players. Side 34 is the advanced side.
cob.startingResources.note: After you determine the starting player, hand out workers clockwise: 1, then 2, 3, and 4. Every player also receives 1 silver coin and 3 random goods tiles.
game.shelfie.name: Shelfie Stacker
game.shelfie.description: Build the best board game shelfie. Each round you draft dice and stack them in the columns of your Big Shelf, chasing tall columns and high top dice. Dice you cannot place go to the Shelf of Shame. After the last round, score the same rows as the official pad.
game.shelfie.footnote: Highest total wins. If tied, the player with the lowest-valued Character Card still in hand wins. If still tied, the tied players share the victory.
shelfie.padHint: Tap a cell and enter how many columns or dice you have. The pad works out the points.
shelfie.fiveTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 5 dice. Each scores 6 points.
shelfie.fourTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 4 dice. Each scores 3 points.
shelfie.threeTallHelper: Count the columns in your Big Shelf with exactly 3 dice. Each scores 1 point.
shelfie.pipsHelper: Add up the pips on the top-most die of each column in your Big Shelf.
shelfie.rewardsHelper: Add the points from any Reward Cards you earned, such as First to Claim and End of Game cards.
shelfie.shameHelper: Count the dice in your Shelf of Shame. Each one costs 2 points.
shelfie.tieTitle: Who has the lowest Character Card?
shelfie.tieMessage: {names} are tied. Choose who has the lowest-valued Character Card still in hand.
shelfie.tieSharedHint: The tied players share the victory, and must say "Shelfie Stacker Sidekick" ten times quickly.
shelfie.setup.boxesBody: In the center of the table, place 1 Delivery Box per player, plus 1 additional Delivery Box. Return the unused Boxes to the, umm, box.
shelfie.setup.diceAll: Place all {n} Dice into the Bag.
shelfie.setup.diceRemove: Remove {n} Dice of each colour ({total} in all) and return them to the box. Place the rest into the Bag.
shelfie.chars.hint: Each player has their own set of 16 Character Cards and keeps 8 of them, returning the others to the box face down. Keep your selected cards hidden from the other players. Tap a card to read its rules.
shelfie.chars.firstGameHint: For your first game, each player uses only cards numbered 1–8. Cards 9–16 are used in the Variants.
shelfie.char.1.name: Bad Lender
shelfie.char.1.rules: This allows you to carry over 1 Dice between rounds or, at the very least, prevent putting 1 into your Shelf of Shame. When removing it from the card, place it into your Box for that round. You can then treat it as if you had just chosen it that round. Dice in your Travel Case at the game’s end do not score any points or count towards the Sidekick Card.
shelfie.char.2.name: Neat Freak
shelfie.char.2.rules: The returned Dice can be taken only from the top-most space of a chosen column (it cannot have Dice placed above it). When returning it, place it into your Box for that round. You can then treat it as if you had just chosen it that round.
shelfie.char.3.name: Upgrade Addict
shelfie.char.3.rules: If using this to affect a Dice in your Big Shelf, it can affect only a Dice in the top-most space of a chosen column (it cannot have Dice placed above it).
shelfie.char.4.name: The Regifter
shelfie.char.4.rules: If returning a Dice from your Big Shelf, it can be taken only from the top-most space of a chosen column (it cannot have Dice placed above it). Dice placed in your Gift Box remain there for the rest of the game and do not score any points, or count towards the Sidekick Card.
shelfie.char.5.name: The Cat
shelfie.char.5.rules: If using this to affect a Dice in your Big Shelf, it can affect only a Dice in the top-most space of a chosen column (it cannot have Dice placed above it). You cannot do this if it would then be of an equal value to the Dice below it.
shelfie.char.6.name: Bargain Hunter
shelfie.char.6.rules: Your dice gets flipped to the number on the opposite side. This would change a 1 to a 6 (Wild), 2 to a 5, 3 to a 4, or vice versa.
shelfie.char.7.name: Monochromist
shelfie.char.7.rules: This lets you break the colour restriction rules when placing the Dice. It does not change the Dice’s colour for other purposes, such as for the Sidekick Card or First to Claim Card. Also, it does not alter the column’s colour for future Dice placed there.
shelfie.char.8.name: Shelfie Snapper
shelfie.char.8.rules: This allows you to take a spent Card and reuse it. This could lead to you having 2 Dice on your Bad Lender or The Regifter. This is totally legal.
shelfie.char.9.name: Con-Questor
shelfie.char.9.rules: This can only be done as you choose your Box, not at the start of a round or after taking your Box. You simply pick up 1 Dice from 1 Box and swap it with 1 Dice from another Box. All Boxes should still have 3 Dice in them after doing so.
shelfie.char.10.name: Dice Chucker
shelfie.char.10.rules: This can be any number of Dice, but the rolled results are final (you cannot revert to what they were originally). Of course, you could always use another Character Card’s ability to alter the rolled values afterwards.
shelfie.char.11.name: Math Trader
shelfie.char.11.rules: This allows you to swap the values of 2 Dice. For example: you might have an Orange 5 and a Blue 2. You could swap their values so that you have an Orange 2 and a Blue 5.
shelfie.char.12.name: The Geek
shelfie.char.12.rules: You still need to follow all normal placement rules. 1 Dice goes straight from your Shelf of Shame, to your Big Shelf (not via your Box). Therefore, some Character Cards might not be legally able to help you alter the Dice’s value (I know you were thinking about it!).
shelfie.char.13.name: The Squisher
shelfie.char.13.rules: This lets you break the numerical placement restriction rules when placing 1 Dice. It does not change the Dice’s number for other purposes, such as the End of Game Cards. Also, it does not alter the placement rules for this column for any future Dice placed.
shelfie.char.14.name: The Playtester
shelfie.char.14.rules: If using this to affect a Dice in your Big Shelf, it can affect only a Dice in the top-most space of a chosen column (it cannot have Dice placed above it). You cannot do this if it would then be of an equal or lower value to the Dice below it.
shelfie.char.15.name: Rad Renter
shelfie.char.15.rules: Take 1 Dice from your Delivery Box and return it to the Dice Bag. Randomly draw 1 Dice from the Bag, set it to any value, and add it to your Box.
shelfie.char.16.name: The Shuffler
shelfie.char.16.rules: This allows you to move multiple adjacent Dice in a single column up 1 space each. After doing so, you must immediately place 1 Dice from your Box into the gap. This Dice must be of the correct colour, plus be higher in value than any Dice below it and lower than those above it. You cannot use the Shuffler’s ability if you do not have a Dice to legally place into the newly created gap.
gwtep.buildings.commonHint: Place the building board near the game board. Sort the common building tiles by their worker cost (top left corner) into 6 stacks and place them next to the corresponding spaces. Once you know the game, turn any number of stacks to the b-side.
gwtep.buildings.neutralHint: Place the El Paso tile on the El Paso space. Then place the 6 neutral building tiles on the 6 neutral building spaces of the game board (B to G).
gwtep.buildings.neutralFirstGame: Each tile on its matching space, B to G.
gwtep.buildings.elPaso: The El Paso tile always goes on the El Paso space.
gwt.trainCards.hint: Place the train below the game board in ascending order of engineers (1–4): the locomotive, then the 3 wagons. Once you know the game, turn some or all cards to their reverse side, marked with a star.
gwt.trainCards.firstGameHint: All cards on their front side.
gwt.cityMaps.hint: Draws side A or B for each city map. Place them above the board: Le Havre on the left, Rotterdam in the middle and Liverpool on the right.
gwt.cityMaps.firstGameHint: All three maps use side A.
gwt.cityMaps.cover: Cover tile on the city center
gwt.setup.nzTilesBody: From the Wellington supply, first pick 1 of each worker type (A back) and place these 4 face up on the indicated spaces of the job market's top row. Then draw {n} more A tiles and place them one after the other.
gwt.setup.nzWorkerBody: The top-most empty space of its column in the job market: the one in its colour with the highest cost. If that column is full, return the tile to its bag and draw a new one.
gwt.setup.nzHazardBody: Its hazard section: the empty space with the lowest number, starting at 1. If that section is full, return the tile to its bag and draw a new one.
gwt.setup.bonusMarketBody: From the Wellington supply, draw tiles with a B on their back (all bonus tiles). Start in the top row under your player count sign and fill rightwards. Continue on the second row from the same column, and stop at the space left of the bonus tiles market token.
gwt.setup.tilesBody: From the Kansas City supply, reveal tiles with a 1 on their back one at a time and place each on the board. Stop once {n} tiles are on the board.
gwt.setup.teepeeBody: Indian trade section: the empty space with the lowest money value, starting at −3.
gwt.setup.outlawBody: Outlaw section: the empty space with the lowest number (1–9).
gwt.setup.hazardBodyBag: Its matching hazard section: the empty space with the lowest number (1–4). If that section is full, return the tile to the bag and draw a new one.
gwt.setup.hazardBody: Its matching hazard section: the empty space with the lowest number (1–4). If that section is full, return the tile face down to the Kansas City supply.
gwt.setup.jobMarketBody: Reveal tiles with a 2 on their back (all workers). Start in the top row under your player count sign and fill rightwards. Continue on the second row from the same column, and stop at the space left of the job market token.
gwt.setup.farmersBody: From the Buenos Aires supply, draw {n} farmer tiles with an A on their back and place them face up on the board, one after the other.
gwt.setup.farmerBody: The area of its color: the empty space with the lowest number (1–4).
gwt.setup.farmerFullBody: If all 4 spaces of that area are taken, return the tile to the bag and draw a new one.
gwt.setup.jobMarketBodyArgentina: From the Buenos Aires supply, draw tiles with a B on their back (all workers). Start in the top row under your player count sign and fill rightwards. Continue on the second row, then the third, each from the same column, and stop at the space left of the job market token.
gwt.setup.shipsBody: On the right side of the board, place the sun ship showing 0 next to Buenos Aires, then the other sun ships below it in ascending order, with the 18 furthest down. Shuffle the remaining ships and put them face down underneath.
gwt.setup.shipsPlainCaption: Shuffled, face down: the ship pile
gwt.setup.citiesBody: Place the maps above the board in the order below. For your first game, use all the a-sides. After that, choose each side randomly or on purpose.
gwt.setup.covers2: Cover the city center of all 3 maps with their matching cover tiles.
gwt.setup.covers3: Cover the city center of Rotterdam with its matching cover tile. Return the other 2 to the box.
gwt.setup.covers4: Return all cover tiles to the box.
game.turing.name: Turing Machine
game.turing.description: Find the secret three-digit code before everyone else. Build a code with the punch cards, test it against the verifiers, and deduce which criterion each verifier checks.
turing.puzzles.intro: The 20 problems from the rulebook. Put each Criteria card in front of its verifier, and the Verification card face down next to it. Problems 01–16 are perfect for new players. Found the code? Hold a puzzle to flip it and see the solution.
turing.puzzles.bankIntro: Offline Challenge Bank #1, sheet {sheet}: {count} puzzles with {verifiers} verifiers. Set them up like the rulebook problems. Hold a puzzle to see its solution and how fast the machine solved it.
turing.puzzles.search: Find a puzzle code, e.g. A41 AA5
turing.hint: Write each round's proposal in the shape cells first. Then tap a verifier box for ✗, tap again for ✓, or hold it for ✓ straight away. The digits on the right work the same way: ✗ crosses a digit out, ✓ circles it.
turing.limit: You can question at most 3 verifiers per round.
turing.handicap.firstRound: Handicap boxes can only be filled in round 1.
turing.handicap.max: The handicap fills at most 2 boxes in round 1.
turing.handicap.title: Handicap mode
turing.handicap.subtitle: For an experienced player: tap up to 2 round 1 boxes to fill them grey. Each counts as a question.
turing.needProposal: Write this round's proposal (all 3 digits) before marking answers.
turing.needProposalDigits: Write your first proposal before marking digits.
turing.finalCode.title: Your code
turing.finalCode.hint: Thumb up? Write the code you found here, secretly, before checking it in the app.
turing.saveImageSaved: Note sheet saved. Check Downloads or your photo gallery.
turing.saveImageFailed: Could not save the note sheet.
turing.clear.title: Clear the note sheet?
turing.clear.body: Everything written on this sheet will be erased.
game.splendor.name: Splendor
game.splendor.description: Collect gems, buy Development cards that give lasting bonuses, and win the favour of nobles. Reaching 15 Prestige points triggers the end of the game.
splendor.setup.gemsAll: Sort the pieces by colour and place all of them within reach of every player, forming 6 stacks.
splendor.setup.gemsRemove: Return {n} pieces of each Gem colour to the box, leaving {left} of each. Keep all 5 Gold pieces. Place the stacks within reach of every player.
splendor.setup.noblesBody: Shuffle the Noble tiles and reveal {n}, one more than the number of players. Line them up above the cards and return the rest to the box.
splendor.setup.cardsBody: Shuffle each Development deck separately. Stack them face down in a column: level 1 at the bottom, level 3 at the top. Reveal 4 cards beside each deck.
game.projectL.name: Project L
game.projectL.description: Fill puzzles with colourful pieces to earn points and bigger pieces. Build an engine of shapes, upgrade your pieces and finish the most valuable puzzles before the Black deck runs out.
projectL.setup.puzzlesBody: Shuffle all 32 White puzzles into a face-down deck. Shuffle the Black puzzles, take {n} at random for the Black deck and return the rest to the box. Reveal the top 4 puzzles of each deck in a row beside it.
projectL.setup.piecesBody: Put all the pieces in a reserve within reach. Each player takes 1 level-1 piece and 1 level-2 piece into their supply.
projectL.rules.intro: Rule changes from the revised (2.0) and 2.5 rulebooks that work with the original box. You can add any of them on its own.
projectL.rules.recycle.title: Recycle (new action)
projectL.rules.recycle.body: Choose a row of puzzles. Put all its puzzles on the bottom of that deck in any order, then reveal 4 new puzzles from the top of the deck to refill the row.
projectL.rules.blindDraw.title: Take from the deck
projectL.rules.blindDraw.body: When you take a puzzle, you may take the top puzzle of either deck instead of one from a row. You can't look at it before you take it.
projectL.rules.runOut.title: When a piece runs out
projectL.rules.runOut.body: If the piece you should take (from an upgrade or a puzzle reward) isn't in the reserve, take another piece of the same level. If that level is empty, take any piece one level higher or any lower level.
projectL.rules.blackLimit.title: Black puzzle limit
projectL.rules.blackLimit.body: Once the Black deck is empty, Black puzzles taken from the row aren't replaced, and each player may take at most 1 Black puzzle per turn until the game ends.
projectL.rules.unfinished.title: Unfinished puzzles cost points
projectL.rules.unfinished.body: At final scoring, subtract the point value of every puzzle you haven't finished.
projectL.rules.faceDown.title: Completed puzzles face down
projectL.rules.faceDown.body: Keep your completed puzzles face down, so scores stay hidden until the end. If everyone agrees before the game, you can keep them face up instead (Known Victory Points).
projectL.rules.finishing.title: Finishing Touches
projectL.rules.finishing.body: Place all your Finishing Touch pieces first; only then are your puzzles completed. You can't finish one puzzle and use its pieces for more Finishing Touches.
projectL.rules.endlessWhite.title: Endless White Deck
projectL.rules.endlessWhite.body: Whenever the White deck runs out, each player writes down the points of their completed White puzzles. Then shuffle all those puzzles into a new White deck.
gwt.elPaso.setup.trainBody: Shuffle the 20 objective tiles and the 20 bonus tiles face down into separate piles near the train. Then draw {n} tiles from each pile and place them face up next to it.
gwt.elPaso.setup.herdBody: Each player takes a set of 10 player cattle cards. Shuffle them and place them face down to the left of your player board as your draw stack, then draw {n} cards into your hand.
gwt.elPaso.hand.note: Unlike other GWT editions, every player draws {n}: later seats don't draw extra cards.
gwt.elPaso.objective.title: Objective Tile
gwt.elPaso.beforeStart.title: Cards & Objective
gwt.elPaso.objective.body: In turn order, each player takes a face-up objective tile and refills it from the pile.
game.alchemists.name: Alchemists
game.alchemists.description: Mix ingredients, test potions and deduce the secret alchemical properties of each ingredient. Publish theories to gain reputation, but beware: a wrong theory can be debunked.
alchemists.logic.intro: Techniques for tracking and solving the deduction puzzle under Alchemists. Open a section to read it; swipe the pictures and tap one to enlarge it.
alchemists.logic.credit: Based on Meeple University's Alchemists logic puzzle tutorial.
alchemists.logic.basics.title: The Basics
alchemists.logic.basics.summary: Ingredients, alchemicals and the mixing rule
alchemists.logic.basics.ingredients: There are **8 ingredients** and **8 alchemicals** (molecules). At the start, the app secretly assigns one alchemical to each ingredient.
alchemists.logic.basics.aspects: Each alchemical has **3 aspects: red, green and blue**. Each aspect is **+ or −** and **large or small**.
alchemists.logic.basics.mixing: **Mixing rule:** find the colour where the two alchemicals have the **same sign but different sizes**. That colour and sign is the potion: a large blue + with a small blue + makes **blue +**.
alchemists.logic.basics.neutral: If no colour matches that way, the potion is **neutral**.
alchemists.logic.reading.title: Reading a Test Result
alchemists.logic.reading.summary: What to cross out after a student test or drinking a potion
alchemists.logic.reading.token: Put the potion token where the two ingredients meet on your results grid.
alchemists.logic.reading.coloured: **Coloured result** (for example blue +): for **both** ingredients, cross out every alchemical with the opposite sign in that colour. That is usually **4 per ingredient**.
alchemists.logic.reading.neutral: **Neutral result:** only **4 alchemical pairs** make neutral. On the deduction sheet they are rows 1+2, 3+4, 5+6 and 7+8.
alchemists.logic.linked.title: Linked Pairs
alchemists.logic.linked.summary: The key technique: letters that cross out squares together
alchemists.logic.linked.why: After a neutral result: if the toad is the row 1 alchemical, the chicken foot **must** be row 2, and the other way round. Each alchemical makes a neutral with exactly one other.
alchemists.logic.linked.letters: So those two grid squares are **linked**. Mark both with the same letter (A, B, C…).
alchemists.logic.linked.follow: Whenever you cross out or confirm a lettered square, **do the same to every square with that letter**.
alchemists.logic.linked.allPairs: Do this for every neutral pair in the two columns. Nothing gets crossed out yet, but later deductions go much faster.
alchemists.logic.selling.title: Selling Potions
alchemists.logic.selling.summary: Earn money and information from adventurers
alchemists.logic.selling.exact: **Exactly correct:** treat it like a test result: token on the grid, then cross out. Follow your linked letters too, and you can learn about an ingredient that **wasn't even in the potion**.
alchemists.logic.selling.partial: **Partly correct (ambiguous)**, for example "sign right, colour wrong" while aiming for green −:
alchemists.logic.selling.partialToken: Use the multi-colour token: the result was **red − or blue −**.
alchemists.logic.selling.partialCross: On its own, it only lets you cross out alchemicals where **both red and blue are +**: just 2 per ingredient.
alchemists.logic.selling.neutral: **Neutral result:** you mixed the neutral potion. Treat it exactly like a neutral result from a test: put the neutral token on your results triangle, and the two ingredients are a neutralizing pair, so all the linked-pair rules apply.
alchemists.logic.selling.wrongSign: **Wrong sign:** both the colour and the sign you aimed for were wrong, so the potion has the **opposite sign**, in an unknown colour.
alchemists.logic.selling.wrongSignToken: Use an uncoloured token: **+** if you were trying to mix a negative potion, **−** if you were trying to mix a positive one.
alchemists.logic.selling.wrongSignCross: A coloured potion needs both ingredients to share its sign in that colour, so **each ingredient has at least one aspect of that sign**. For both ingredients, cross out the alchemical whose aspects are all the opposite sign: **red +, green +, blue +** after a − result, or **red −, green −, blue −** after a + result.
alchemists.logic.thinking.title: Critical Thinking
alchemists.logic.thinking.summary: Deductions that combine what the grid already shows
alchemists.logic.thinking.sameColour: **An ingredient can't make + and − of the same colour.** If the scorpion already made blue +, an ambiguous "red − or blue −" with the scorpion must be **red −**.
alchemists.logic.thinking.sizes: **Sizes tell you about the partner.** If only small blue + options remain for the scorpion, both ingredients it made blue + with must have a **large** blue +, so cross out their small ones.
alchemists.logic.thinking.twoOptions: **Two ingredients down to the same two options:** link them with a new letter, and cross those two alchemicals out for **every other ingredient**, or you would run out of options. This often happens when two ingredients make the same potion with the same third ingredient.
alchemists.logic.thinking.foundRow: **Once an ingredient is found, cross out its row** for all the others: each alchemical belongs to only one ingredient.
alchemists.logic.thinking.twoOfEach: **Two of each:** mixed with the other 7, every alchemical makes **exactly 2 red, 2 green, 2 blue and 1 neutral** potion. So if an ingredient already made two blue + potions, an ambiguous "green + or blue +" must be **green +**.
alchemists.logic.theories.title: Publishing Theories
alchemists.logic.theories.summary: When it's safe to hedge, confirm or debunk
alchemists.logic.theories.hedged: **Hedged theory:** when an ingredient is down to 2 options, find the colour where they differ. If both have red − and blue − but green differs, publish a theory **hedged on green**.
alchemists.logic.theories.confirmed: **Confirmed theory:** once an ingredient has only 1 option left.
alchemists.logic.theories.debunk: **Debunking** (Apprentice mode) reveals the sign of one aspect of one ingredient. It is **public**: every player can cross out with it.
alchemists.logic.debunking.title: Learning from Debunking
alchemists.logic.debunking.summary: Every attempt is public, even other players'
alchemists.logic.debunking.public: Every debunking attempt is **public**, including other players' attempts. Everyone can record what the card reader shows, so watch them all.
alchemists.logic.debunking.masterYes: **Master variant:** a player picks two ingredients and a potion, and the card reader says whether they make it. A **yes** is a full experiment result for everyone: record it like your own.
alchemists.logic.debunking.masterNo: A **no** is weaker: it only rules out that one potion for the pair. Note it and come back to it when your grid narrows down.
alchemists.logic.debunking.anyIngredient: In Master debunking **your hand isn't used**, so you can test **any two ingredients**, even ones you don't hold. A valid demonstration doubles as an extra experiment, and earns +2 reputation if it debunks a theory or shows a new conflict. It must still be able to do one of those, or it costs 1 reputation.
alchemists.logic.debunking.bothAnswers: Choose demonstrations where **either answer** teaches you something.
alchemists.logic.planning.title: Planning Experiments
alchemists.logic.planning.summary: Choose mixes that can only give one answer
alchemists.logic.planning.predict: Before mixing, work out what each remaining option **would** produce with each partner you could use.
alchemists.logic.planning.pick: Pick the partner that gives a **different result for every option**: one experiment then identifies the ingredient. Here, flower + chicken foot could be ambiguous, while flower + mushroom tells all three options apart.
alchemists.logic.strategy.title: Protect Your Information
alchemists.logic.strategy.summary: Results are public, so keep your inputs secret
alchemists.logic.strategy.public: Every result from the app is **public**, so keep your **inputs** secret.
alchemists.logic.strategy.worst: **Worst move:** taking two face-up ingredient cards and testing them right away. Everyone learns what you just spent 3 actions on.
alchemists.logic.strategy.bigHand: Keep a **big hand** of ingredient cards and bluff about what you're mixing.
alchemists.logic.strategy.sevenExperimen: An efficient solve takes about **7 experiments**, so don't give them away for free.
alchemists.logic.strategy.trust: Build on **other players' theories** to move faster, but they may be **deliberately hedged**.
alchemists.setup.gold: Gold pieces, on your player board
alchemists.setup.ingredients: Ingredient cards, from the top of the deck
alchemists.setup.firstRound: In the first round everyone uses only {first} action cubes. Put the other {rest} on the adventurer stack, to remember to take them all at the end of the first round.
alchemists.master.intro: Everything that changes when you play Alchemists as Masters. In short: you start with 2 ingredients, use the stricter conference side, and debunk with proof by experiment, which brings conflict tokens. Everything else is the same.
alchemists.master.choosing.title: Choosing the Variant
alchemists.master.choosing.summary: When to play Master, and what changes
alchemists.master.choosing.first: For your **first game**, play Apprentice: its rules are a little simpler and its conferences more forgiving, yet it still offers the full range of possibilities.
alchemists.master.choosing.differences: There are only **3 differences**: the ingredient cards at the start, the conference tiles, and the debunking rules.
alchemists.master.setup.title: Setup
alchemists.master.setup.summary: Ingredients, conference tiles, conflict tokens and the app
alchemists.master.setup.ingredients: Each Master draws **2 ingredient cards** from the top of the deck (Apprentices draw 3).
alchemists.master.setup.conferences: Use the **wizard hat side** of the conference tiles. Masters are held to higher standards at conferences.
alchemists.master.setup.conflict: The **6 conflict tokens** are used only in the Master variant.
alchemists.master.setup.app: Select **Master** in the card reader before tapping Start New Game.
alchemists.master.debunking.title: Master Debunking
alchemists.master.debunking.summary: Prove a theory wrong with an experiment
alchemists.master.debunking.proof: It isn't enough to know **which aspect** is wrong: you need **an experiment that proves it**.
alchemists.master.debunking.how1: Tap Debunk Theory and set the card reader where everyone can see it. It shows the 8 ingredients.
alchemists.master.debunking.how2: **Your hand isn't used.** Select any **two ingredients**, then one of the seven potions.
alchemists.master.debunking.how3: **Before confirming**, explain how each answer ("they **do** make it" or "they **don't**") would **debunk a theory** or **show a new conflict**.
alchemists.master.debunking.success: **Success** (a debunked theory or a new conflict): **+2 reputation**.
alchemists.master.debunking.wrongVariant: Debunking works differently in each variant. If the card reader is set to the wrong one, go back to the main menu, change it and tap Continue Game.
alchemists.master.oneTwo.title: Debunking One or Two Theories
alchemists.master.oneTwo.one: **One theory**, the common case: show that one aspect of one ingredient is the opposite of its published theory. You gain 2, and the seal owners take the usual penalties, except seals hedged against that colour.
alchemists.master.oneTwo.two: **Two theories:** if both ingredients in your demonstration have published theories, one experiment can debunk both.
alchemists.master.oneTwo.penalties: Reveal the seals on both and add up each player's penalties: losing 5 on each counts as **one loss of 10**, which matters for the reputation zones.
alchemists.master.oneTwo.reward: Your reward is still only **+2**, with only **one** immediate publication.
alchemists.master.conflict.title: Conflicts
alchemists.master.conflict.summary: When two theories can't both be true
alchemists.master.conflict.what: Your result can show that two theories **can't both be true** without showing which one is wrong. Either answer can do this; sometimes "they don't" is the success.
alchemists.master.conflict.reward: That is worth **+2 reputation**. **Nobody loses points**, and there is **no immediate publication**.
alchemists.master.conflict.mark: Mark both theories with **matching conflict tokens**.
alchemists.master.conflict.seals: Their seals stay, but **no longer count** for **conferences, grants or the top alchemist award**, and **no one can endorse** them.
alchemists.master.conflict.reuse: They can still be used in later debunking attempts, including a demonstration of a **different** conflict.
alchemists.master.conflict.clear: If either theory is debunked, remove both conflict tokens: the other theory is normal again (even if it might still be wrong).
alchemists.master.conflict.scoring: Conflict tokens don't matter at final scoring: seals score their points either way.
alchemists.master.invalid.title: Invalid Demonstrations
alchemists.master.invalid.rule: Your ingredients and potion must be able to **debunk at least one specific theory** or **show a new two-theory conflict**.
alchemists.master.invalid.back: If neither is possible, press **back** and rethink. Going ahead counts as a failed attempt: **−1 reputation**.
alchemists.master.invalid.example: For example, proving something about two ingredients that have **no published theories** proves nothing specific, so it is invalid.
alchemists.master.invalid.repeat: A conflict already marked with conflict tokens isn't new: **−1 reputation**.
alchemists.master.round.title: End of Round and Scoring
alchemists.master.round.award: **Top alchemist award:** don't count seals on theories with conflict tokens.
alchemists.master.round.conference: **Conferences:** count all seals except those on theories in conflict.
alchemists.master.grid.title: Using the Deduction Grid
alchemists.master.grid.positive: Debunking demonstrations are public. A positive one (for example, another player shows mushroom + toad make red +) can be recorded like your own experiment.
alchemists.master.grid.negative: A negative one ("they don't make blue −") is harder to use; you'll need your own way to note it.
alchemists.master.mixing.title: Mixing the Variants
alchemists.master.mixing.summary: Combine rules, or even out experience
alchemists.master.mixing.free: Mix the rules freely: for example, start with 2 ingredients and use Apprentice conferences, but debunk by the Master rules.
alchemists.master.mixing.equalizer: As an equalizer, a newer player can start with 3 ingredients while everyone else takes 2. The conference tiles can be flipped for each player, and the app can switch between Apprentice and Master during debunking.
game.century.name: Century: Spice Road
game.century.description: Lead a caravan along the Spice Road: play merchant cards to gather, upgrade and trade spices, then deliver them to claim point cards.
century.setup.pointsBody: Shuffle the orange-backed point cards into a deck and lay {cards} face up to its left. Put {n} gold coins above the leftmost card and {n} silver coins above the second.
century.setup.merchantsBody: Take out the purple-bordered starting cards, then shuffle the other merchant cards into a deck and lay {cards} face up to its left.
century.setup.toBox: {n} starting cards back to the box
century.setup.spicesBody: Sort the cubes into the bowls in upgrade order. The supply is unlimited: if a colour runs out, use a substitute.
century.start.createHint: Starting card in your hand: take 2 yellow cubes
century.start.upgradeHint: Starting card in your hand: upgrade cubes 2 levels
century.start.caravanHint: Holds up to {n} cubes at the end of your turn
century.start.spicesBody: Place these cubes on your caravan card. Seats count clockwise from the first player.
century.start.spicesNote: Later seats start with a little more to make up for playing later.
century.score.finalBody: When the game ends, each player adds up:
century.score.cardsHint: The value printed on each card you claimed
century.score.cubesHint: Each one left on your caravan
century.score.endBody: When a player claims this point card, finish the current round so everyone gets the same number of turns, then score.
century.score.tie: Ties go to the tied player who took their turn last, the one furthest from the first player in turn order.
game.centuryEw.name: Century: Eastern Wonders
game.centuryEw.description: Sail the islands of the Far East: trade spices at markets, build outposts, and deliver cargo to ports to claim VP tiles.
centuryEw.setup.mapBody: Sort the market tiles by trade symbol and randomly remove 1 of each symbol. Shuffle the rest and build the map: the rulebook's pattern for your first game, your own design later, with each tile next to at least 2 others. Put the {ports} port tiles at the corners.
centuryEw.setup.toBox: {n} market tiles back to the box
centuryEw.setup.vpBody: Set the Closed Port tile aside and shuffle the VP tiles face down. Put 1 face up on each of the {ports} ports. Then shuffle the Closed Port tile, face down, into the next {n} tiles and put these {top} back on top of the pile.
centuryEw.setup.bonusBody: Sort the bonus tiles by type. Stack the VP bonus tiles in order with the 6 on top, then 5, 4 and 3.
centuryEw.setup.spicesBody: Sort the cubes into the bowls in upgrade order.
centuryEw.start.boardHint: Eastern Wonders side up. The first player (whoever was last on a boat) takes the board with the first-player icon.
centuryEw.start.boatHint: Placed on a market tile when you choose your starting cubes
centuryEw.start.outpostsHint: In your colour, one on each space of your player board
centuryEw.start.cargoHint: Discard down to it at the end of every turn
centuryEw.start.cubesBody: Put the {n} starting cube sets in the middle of the table. In reverse turn order, each player takes one set, puts it in their cargo hold and places their boat on any market tile.
centuryEw.start.cubesNote: The last player chooses first. Return the sets nobody took to the supply.
centuryEw.score.endBody: When a player claims their {n}th VP tile, finish the current round so everyone gets the same number of turns, then score.
centuryEw.score.vpTilesHint: The value on each VP tile you claimed at a port
centuryEw.score.boardHint: The values uncovered where you built outposts
centuryEw.score.bonusVpHint: Its value: the 6 goes first, then 5, 4 and 3
centuryEw.score.harvestHint: The one that adds a red cube to Harvest
centuryEw.score.upgradeHint: The one that upgrades a cube after building an outpost
centuryEw.score.cubesHint: Each one left in your cargo hold
